claims.text: Adding a high-entropy alloy component to single-phase ZrB2 will form a composite material.
The proposed ZrB2–HEA composite will require a lower preparation temperature than single-phase ZrB2.
The HEA component will improve the oxidation resistance of the composite.
The HEA component will improve the high-temperature stability of the composite.
The proposed composite will have better oxidation resistance than single-phase ZrB2.
The proposed composite will have better high-temperature stability than single-phase ZrB2.
The proposed composite will outperform prior lower-temperature specimens in oxidation resistance and high-temperature stability.
The intervention can overcome vulnerability to corrosion by liquid plating metal during prolonged bath service.
The proposed composite can retain adequate strength and structural integrity under the stated manufacturing and service conditions.
HEB#1 exhibited better oxidation behavior than most of its individually fabricated diboride components, including ZrB2, under identical processing.
HEB#1 and HEB#7 maintained their shapes at 1500 °C.
Hardness and oxidation measurements were performed on high-entropy diborides and individual metal-diboride benchmarks fabricated by the same HEBM and SPS process parameters, apart from CrB2.
Composite specimens with varying HEA compositions and preparation temperatures should be tested for oxidation resistance, high-temperature stability, and mechanical properties.
Failure to improve oxidation resistance, high-temperature stability, and preparation temperature relative to the stated baselines would falsify the hypothesis.
The exact HEA composition, properties, and optimal preparation conditions are uncertain.
